derived.fact: The Moon does not orbit Venus.
chain: Before the edit: the Moon orbits Earth, and a moon orbits one planet, so it does not orbit Venus.
The reason for 'no' was the removed fact: nobody writes that the Moon does not orbit Venus, so no separately stored fact rules it out.
So whether the Moon orbits Venus is not known.

So the gas that makes up most of that planet's atmosphere is not known.

The Moon orbits Earth..why: Stated everywhere, in these words and as "the Moon orbits the Earth"; Wikipedia says it in its Moon article. A model holds it directly; it follows from nothing else it knows.

sources.quote: It orbits Earth in an elliptical path, at a distance  that varies over the year, averaging around 378,000 kilometers (235,000 mi).

The atmosphere of the planet that the Mo.why: Nobody gives the atmosphere of a planet through its moon: people say what Earth's air is made of, and which planet the Moon orbits, but not the two together. The direct form is absent and the description "planet that the Moon orbits" is itself almost never written, while the orbit premise is stated thousands of times.

The body that the Apollo 11 astronauts w.why: Apollo 11 is described by the Moon it landed on, and the Moon by the planet it orbits, but nobody chains the two into one sentence about "the body the astronauts walked on". The direct form is absent; each link is stated often.

Earth has a natural satellite..why: Stated in every introduction to Earth: Earth has one natural satellite, the Moon. It is the same fact as 'the Moon orbits Earth' only after the inverse and the 'only satellite' reading, and people write it as a sentence of its own.

notes: Template: ABox contraction on a functional relation (orbits). Removes "The Moon orbits Earth", the original fact of physics-replace-0001, a stored fact. Cardinality question: another planet (Venus) the Moon does not orbit; "no" before because a moon orbits one planet, "does not know" after because the reason for "no" is gone. Related near uses the inverse (orbits is tagged inverse:orbited_by): Earth's only natural satellite. Related far is the revision's question about the planet the Moon orbits (stored fact: Earth is the third planet from the Sun). The two 2-hop derived questions go through the removed fact by description (composition: the atmosphere of the planet the Moon orbits) and by an alias for the subject (binding: the body the Apollo 11 astronauts walked on); both derived answers are worked out, not stated. The subject is "the Moon" in all queries, as in the revision. The near prompt says "natural satellite" rather than "moon" so it does not repeat the edit's verb.
